summary: The first public release, and the first on the Microsoft Store.
features: Storage you already have: Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2 and MinIO, a local folder or NAS, Telegram, GitHub (served through jsDelivr), Google Drive, OneDrive and WebDAV. Use several, and pick one per video.
Move a published video from one storage to another.
Batches: group a whole season, run it in order, and see every episode's stage on a live board.
Pause and resume a video or a whole batch, and convert several videos at once.
Subtitles (.srt, .vtt) in any language and a poster of your own, also added later to a video that is already online.
Series catalog in English and Khmer, with TMDB lookup and Gemini translation using your own keys.
Telegram with just a bot token and a channel ID, and those videos play in iVault's own preview.
Windows builds for x64 and Arm64, on the Microsoft Store and as a direct installer.
fixes: A failed Telegram upload resumes with only the files that are left, instead of sending the whole video again.
Converting on Windows works: two Windows-only problems made FFmpeg stop with "Permission denied".
notes: On Windows, a pause takes effect after the current step (for example, when encoding finishes) rather than instantly.
Telegram accepts files up to 20 MB each, so iVault publishes one quality there instead of several.
Removing a video from iVault, or moving it to other storage, does not delete the files already uploaded.
A Google Drive connection needs renewing every 7 days while your Google OAuth app is in testing mode; OneDrive about every 90 days.

features: Convert a video to HLS at 360p, 480p, 720p and 1080p with FFmpeg, and get one master.m3u8 link.
Upload to Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO or a local folder, then check every file is reachable before calling the job done.
Dashboard, Library, video details with a preview player, and a step-by-step New video wizard.
A transfer dock with live progress, cancel and retry.
Storage keys kept in the system keychain, never in a file.
One-click FFmpeg install on macOS and Linux.
fixes: A failed check now names the files that are missing, instead of only counting them.
Exporting the catalog no longer overwrites a series' other episodes.
A queued video can be removed from the Library.
notes: On Windows, FFmpeg is installed by hand.
No pause yet, and no time-left estimate.
